answer: Interleaved arrival shaping. A new identity's first transactions must arrive spaced across a randomized multi-hour window, and bursts flagged as a raven cluster get throttled to one op per interval. Honest users accumulate history on an island of steady traffic, while attackers needing many identities must simulate idle gaps on every one. Sustained spacing at the zenith of throughput costs an attacker thousands of concurrent sleeping sessions and wall-clock days per batch, so throughput scales with elapsed time, not capital.
